APIs & logs · MCP integration

Connect your HTTP API to AI without handing over its API key.

Expose a selected HTTP service through an MCP endpoint. GateRook adds the connection’s authentication, constrains destinations and paths, and separates read requests from requests that need approval. Use it for internal APIs or services with an HTTP interface.

Understand the request flow

Ask your AI

Fetch order 48213 from the stage API and report its status. Do not retry or modify it.

http_get · arguments
{
  "connection": "stage-api",

}
Example result
{
  "status": 200,

    "id": 48213,

}

Sample configuration and output, not a live connection. Replace example values with your environment. Tool names here are connector names; the endpoint may expose a connection-specific name.

Put context to work

What you can do with HTTP API and AI

Ask about an internal API response

Read an order or service status through a narrowly allowed route. The AI receives the response while GateRook attaches the required authentication.

Compare API and database state

Expose an API connection alongside a read-only database connection to investigate differences between the application view and stored records.

Review a proposed service change

Use http_request for a supported write method. GateRook shows the actual request for approval before sending a permitted mutation.

From service to MCP

How to connect HTTP API

GateRook must be running on a computer that can reach your service. Open Connections, choose Add connection, and select HTTP API. Give the connection a name and environment.

New to GateRook? Start with the full setup guide.
  1. 01

    Choose an API scope and credential

    Identify the HTTPS base URL and the specific routes needed for the task. Obtain a service credential with appropriately limited permissions and identify any GET routes that change state.

  2. 02

    Configure the HTTP connection

    Open Connections, choose Add connection and HTTP API. Set base URLs and allowed paths. Select the authentication type and enter its token, API key or password in the connection form.

  3. 03

    Set transport and test behavior

    Use the server’s TLS configuration, adding a private CA when necessary. Configure a safe test path. Test connection may identify required network allowlist or certificate settings for you to review.

  4. 04

    Test and choose the exposed tools

    Run Test connection, then finish Add to endpoint. Expose http_get for reads. Enable http_request only when you intend to review actions that may change service state.

  5. 05

    Choose the endpoint and tool modes

    Add the tested connection to an endpoint. In Tools & policies, enable only the tools needed for the task. Start with Read only where supported; use Approval for any selected mutation and leave other tools Off. A connection alone does not grant an AI client access.

  6. 06

    Connect your AI and verify the first call

    In Clients, choose your AI app and endpoint, review the connection details, and connect. Try this guide’s example in Playground before asking your AI. Open Activity to inspect the tool, target, decision and returned result. The getting started guide covers this shared flow.

Connection settings

Configure HTTP API in GateRook

These are example values for the connection form. Enter credentials into GateRook’s secret fields, not into an AI prompt. Requirements and alternatives are noted per field.

HTTP API connection configuration
SettingExampleHow to use it
Name / environmentstage-api / stageChoose HTTP API in Connections.
Base URLshttps://api.stage.internalRequests must remain under a configured base URL, including any base path.
Allowed paths/v1/orders/**Path globs restrict which routes the agent may access.
Credentials typebearerSupported modes: none, bearer, API key in a header, API key in the query, and basic authentication.
TokenEnter in GateRook (write-only)The gateway adds Authorization. The agent does not need to supply the service token.
GET paths that change state/v1/orders/*/retryMark side-effecting GET routes. http_get refuses them; http_request requires approval.
Test path/v1/orders?limit=1Use a safe GET or HEAD path for the connection test.

Know what you expose

HTTP API tools and access boundaries

The connector determines what is possible. Endpoint modes and connection policies determine what a particular AI client may use.

Available tools and access behavior
ToolPurposeAccess behavior
http_getSend GET or HEAD to permitted routes with authentication supplied by GateRook. Off by default on prod.Read only
http_requestSend a supported HTTP method. Requests classified as mutations require approval.Approval

Before you enable access

  • Allowed base URLs and paths constrain destinations. This connector is not an unrestricted web browser or arbitrary network proxy.
  • A GET route is not automatically harmless: configure any known side-effecting GET paths explicitly.
  • Production disallows query-string API keys, plain HTTP and same-origin redirect following. Redirect following is off by default.
  • HTTP response size and execution limits apply. The remote service’s credential permissions remain authoritative.

GateRook stores local connection secrets encrypted and resolves them for connectors. Allowed tool results are returned to your AI client and may be processed by its provider. Scope the data you expose as well as the actions you allow.

Practical answers

HTTP API connection questions

Use Test connection to isolate service access problems. Use Playground and Activity to inspect endpoint permissions and tool calls.

Can I connect an API without a dedicated MCP server?

Yes. GateRook’s HTTP connector exposes generic HTTP tools over MCP and adds the configured service authentication. Define the permitted base URLs and paths before connecting the AI app.

Can I create named tools from an OpenAPI definition?

The core supports OpenAPI templates for an existing HTTP connection, but this desktop build does not yet offer OpenAPI import in Connectors. The setup in this guide uses the available http_get and http_request tools.

Can the agent see my API key?

The configured secret is added by GateRook when it sends the request. Do not put it in the prompt or tool arguments. Response content is still service data, so expose only routes appropriate for your AI app.

What happens to a GET endpoint that changes data?

Add its path to GET paths that change state. http_get will refuse it, and an otherwise permitted http_request requires human approval.
